---
title: "Many-facet GPCM: measurement and rating agreement"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
params:
  ratings_csv: null
  rating_min: 1
  rating_max: 4
  output_dir: "gpcm-report-files"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(mfrmr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5)
example_run <- is.null(params$ratings_csv)
if (example_run) {
  ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
} else {
  ratings <- read.csv(params$ratings_csv, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE)
  stopifnot(all(c("Person", "Rater", "Criterion", "Score") %in% names(ratings)))
  score <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ratings$Score))
  if (any(!is.na(ratings$Score) & is.na(score)))
    stop("Score must contain numeric rubric values or NA. Recode documented missing markers first.")
  ratings$Score <- score
}
rubric <- seq.int(params$rating_min, params$rating_max)
if (anyDuplicated(ratings[c("Person", "Rater", "Criterion")]))
  stop("This template expects one rating per Person/Rater/Criterion. For repeated occasions, define the measurement unit and agreement keys explicitly.")

fit <- fit_mfrm(
  ratings, person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"), score = "Score",
  rating_min = params$rating_min, rating_max = params$rating_max,
  category_policy = "preserve", method = "MML", model = "GPCM",
  step_facet = "Criterion", slope_facet = "Criterion"
)
diagnostics <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, diagnostic_mode = "both", residual_pca = "none")
results <- mfrm_results(fit, diagnostics = diagnostics, include = "publication")
study_context <- c(
  rating_unit = "One Person by Rater by Criterion rating",
  score_direction = "Specify what higher coded scores mean in this study",
  rubric = paste("Permitted scores", params$rating_min, "to", params$rating_max),
  transformation = "No recoding in this template; document any prior transformation"
)
report <- mfrm_report(results, style = "apa", study_context = study_context)
fit_summary <- summary(fit)
alpha <- krippendorff_alpha_table(
  ratings, rater = "Rater", unit = c("Person", "Criterion"), score = "Score",
  level = "ordinal", categories = rubric
)
curves <- category_curves_report(fit, digits = 15)
out <- params$output_dir
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Relate this report to the assessment question

When combining measurement and G/D studies, report each analysis's input unit,
retained sample, score scale, facets, aggregation, weights and uncertainty
separately. Explain what MFRM reveals about specific facet effects and what
G/D reveals about reproducibility of the defined observed score and future
plans. Do not treat Rasch-adjusted estimates as interchangeable with raw G-study
scores. The package's `mfrmr-networks-and-reporting` vignette shows published
speaking/writing examples and a FACETS/ConQuest reporting crosswalk. Select
linking, bias and model-comparison modules from `mfrmr-reporting-and-apa` when
they address the question; this template does not run every possible analysis.

## Read this report

`r if (example_run) "**Synthetic example:** this report illustrates the workflow; its numbers are not findings about a real assessment." else "**Study draft:** complete the context and interpretation prompts before using this report in a manuscript."`

This report separates three questions: how persons and raters differ on the
measurement scale, how closely ratings follow the model, and how much raters
agree on observed scores. It includes the tables, two figures and underlying
files needed to develop a Methods and Results section.

**Current analysis:** `r report$decision$Interpretation[1]`.
**Formal-inference status:** `r report$decision$FormalInference[1]`.
This status is retained in the saved analysis. A review status does not turn
the descriptive tables into confirmatory evidence.

## Study question and rating design

**Complete for your study:** state the assessment purpose and intended score
use, participants and recruitment, rater selection/training, assignment and
overlap, and the substantive meaning of each rubric category. Explain why
criterion-specific thresholds and discriminations address the question.
Record both endpoint labels and which direction answers the substantive
question. Comprehensibility can mean ease or difficulty; the column name
does not determine that direction. Retain any recoding rule and the original
scores, and ensure anchors use the same coding and scale.

```{r design}
design <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Input rating rows", "Retained model rows", "Retained persons",
    "Retained raters", "Retained criteria", "Input missing scores"),
  Value = c(nrow(ratings), nrow(fit$prep$data),
    length(unique(fit$prep$data$Person)), length(unique(fit$prep$data$Rater)),
    length(unique(fit$prep$data$Criterion)), sum(is.na(ratings$Score)))
)
knitr::kable(design, caption = "Analysis units and data retention")
```

Rows are repeated ratings, not independent participants. Describe missing or
excluded ratings and their reasons from the study records; absent planned
assignments require an assignment roster to identify.

## Model and estimation

A one-family many-facet GPCM was fitted by marginal maximum likelihood (MML),
with criterion-specific category steps and discriminations, fixed rater and
criterion effects, and an estimated normal person-population mean and SD.
Relative criterion slopes have geometric mean one. Facet locations are
centered within each facet. Higher Person locations predict higher coded
scores; higher default Rater locations predict lower coded scores, meaning
stricter scoring only when higher scores are more favorable. The permitted score scale was
`r params$rating_min`–`r params$rating_max`, including unused permitted categories.

```{r fit-settings}
knitr::kable(fit_summary$overview[, intersect(c("Model", "Method", "Persons",
  "Converged", "LogLik"), names(fit_summary$overview)), drop = FALSE], digits = 3)
knitr::kable(fit_summary$settings_overview[, intersect(c("QuadPoints",
  "RatingMin", "RatingMax"), names(fit_summary$settings_overview)), drop = FALSE])
population <- fit_summary$population_overview
population_coefficients <- fit_summary$population_coefficients
knitr::kable(population[, c("Formula", "IdentificationRole", "ResidualVariance",
  "InferenceReady")], digits = 3, caption = "Recorded population model and variance")
knitr::kable(population_coefficients, digits = 3,
  caption = "Estimated population mean (intercept); no interval is supplied here")
```

Retain the numerical review below. If an interval or close model comparison is
central to the conclusion, perform and report its target-specific checks.
Changing the model, prior, anchors, weights or estimator requires updating this
Methods description as well as the code.

## Estimates and discrimination

```{r estimates}
measures <- as.data.frame(diagnostics$measures)
slopes <- as.data.frame(fit$slopes)
knitr::kable(subset(measures, Facet != "Person", select = c(
  Facet, Level, Estimate, SE, SEUse)), digits = 3,
  caption = "Rater and criterion locations, with the recorded SE-use status")
knitr::kable(slopes[, c("SlopeFacet", "Estimate", "ParameterStatus", "CIEligible")],
  digits = 3, caption = "Criterion discrimination estimates and interval eligibility")
```

The slope describes sensitivity to ability on the declared scale. It is not
a scoring weight or a ranking of criterion quality. No slope intervals are
computed by this template; request and review `confint(fit, parm = "slopes")`
separately when they answer the study question. Step estimates and all Person
measures are retained in the exported tables.

## Separation, Strata and reliability

```{r precision}
precision <- as.data.frame(diagnostics$reliability)
knitr::kable(precision[, c("Facet", "Levels", "Separation", "Strata",
  "Reliability", "RealReliability", "ReliabilityUse")], digits = 3,
  caption = "Separation-based precision summaries by facet")
```

Person separation concerns distinguishable abilities; rater separation
concerns distinguishable severities. High rater separation reliability does
not mean high agreement. Strata is a transformation of separation, not an
observed number of groups. Model and fit-adjusted reliability use different
error bases; the GPCM summaries here use approximate marginal-SE variance
subtraction without propagating covariance. Retain their recorded use status.

**Results prompt:** explain which facet matters for the research question,
the magnitude of its differences and whether the available precision supports
the intended interpretation. Do not label every coefficient simply “reliability.”

## Model fit

```{r fit-statistics}
fit_table <- as.data.frame(diagnostics$fit)
knitr::kable(subset(fit_table, Facet != "Person", select = c(
  Facet, Level, N, Infit, Outfit, InfitZSTD, OutfitZSTD, FitStatus)), digits = 3,
  caption = "Rater and criterion fit; all Person rows are retained in the CSV")
```

These Infit/Outfit statistics use native MML EAP plug-in diagnostics. They are
not numerically interchangeable with posterior-averaged TAM/ConQuest fit.
MnSq has reference value 1; any screening cutoff needs a stated purpose and
source. Review flags prompt investigation rather than automatic exclusions.

## Wright map

```{r wright-map, fig.cap="Person EAPs, rater/criterion locations and category steps for this GPCM. This point-estimate map does not display confidence intervals."}
png(file.path(out, "wright.png"), width = 1800, height = 1200, res = 200)
tryCatch(wright <- plot(fit, type = "wright", diagnostics = diagnostics,
  show_ci = FALSE, top_n = Inf, preset = "publication"), finally = dev.off())
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(out, "wright.png"))
```

**Results prompt:** describe targeting and the size of relevant facet
differences. This map does not establish unidimensionality or test every
rater contrast.

## Category-probability curves

```{r probability-curves, fig.cap="Category probabilities conditional on ability for the fitted criterion profiles. Additive facet locations are fixed at the reference value zero; these are point curves, not confidence bands."}
png(file.path(out, "ccc.png"), width = 1800, height = 1200, res = 200)
tryCatch(ccc <- plot(fit, type = "ccc", preset = "publication"), finally = dev.off())
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(out, "ccc.png"))
```

The curves show where each permitted score is most probable. Their owners and
reference settings are retained below and with the exported coordinates.
Use `category_curves_report(fit, newdata = ...)` for specified full rating
contexts rather than interpreting a reference profile as an average rating.

```{r curve-profiles}
knitr::kable(curves$curve_profiles, caption = "Category-curve profiles")
```

## Observed rating agreement

```{r agreement}
knitr::kable(alpha$table[, c("Alpha", "Level", "Status", "Raters", "Units",
  "PairableUnits", "PairableRatings")], digits = 3,
  caption = "Ordinal Krippendorff's alpha on matched Person × Criterion units")
```

Alpha is calculated from observed ratings, separately from the GPCM. Report
the ordinal distance definition, pairable units and ratings, and how missing
ratings were handled. Units with fewer than two nonmissing ratings do not
contribute to alpha. This output provides no confidence interval. Alpha is
neither Cronbach's alpha nor the separation reliability above.

**Results prompt:** explain the observed agreement and its practical relevance
alongside the model-adjusted severity differences; neither alone establishes
validity or individual rater accuracy.

### Optional: agreement for specified rater pairs

The example above asks about the panel. If your question concerns particular
pairs, use Cohen's kappa with an explicitly chosen weighting. This code is
provided for adaptation and is not run automatically:

```{r pairwise-agreement, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
kappa <- pairwise_kappa_table(
  ratings, rater = "Rater", unit = c("Person", "Criterion"), score = "Score",
  categories = rubric, weights = "quadratic"
)
kappa$table[, c("Rater1", "Rater2", "N", "Kappa", "Status")]
write.csv(kappa$table, file.path(out, "pairwise_kappa.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(kappa, file.path(out, "pairwise_kappa.rds"))
```

Choose unweighted, linear or quadratic weights from the category meaning.
`N` counts shared complete units for each pair; pairs without overlap retain
unavailable values. Do not average pairwise kappas into a panel coefficient
or choose pairs/weights after seeing which coefficients are largest. For
different criteria or occasions, decide whether separate analyses are needed.
Separation, Strata and Reliability above describe a different question and
remain part of the measurement report.

## Files and references

```{r save-files}
tables <- list(study_context = report$study_context, design = design, measures = measures, slopes = slopes,
  population = population, population_coefficients = population_coefficients,
  steps = as.data.frame(fit$steps), precision = precision, fit = fit_table,
  ordinal_alpha = alpha$table, alpha_units = alpha$unit_summary,
  curve_profiles = curves$curve_profiles, curve_coordinates = curves$probabilities)
for (name in names(tables))
  write.csv(tables[[name]], file.path(out, paste0(name, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(report$markdown, file.path(out, "report-draft.md"))
saveRDS(list(results = results, report = report, agreement = alpha, curves = curves,
  plots = list(wright = wright, ccc = ccc)), file.path(out, "analysis.rds"))
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(out, "session-info.txt"))
knitr::kable(data.frame(File = list.files(out)), caption = "Saved analysis files")
```

The CSVs retain the returned values; displayed tables are rounded. The RDS retains
the fit, diagnostics, agreement audits and report with declared score meaning.
Review identifiers before sharing.
Add the model and agreement-method references relevant to your actual analysis;
see `?fit_mfrm`, `?krippendorff_alpha_table` and `?mfrmr_methods_reference`.
